\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of the all-negative input]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_neg_one}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_neg_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.andFunction, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $w$, the uniform probability that the AND function on the
sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^w$ outputs $-1$ is $2^{-w}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of a positive AND output]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_one}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.andFunction, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_neg_one, FABL.uniformProbability_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative integer $w$, the uniform probability that the AND function on the
sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^w$ outputs $1$ is $1-2^{-w}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes with zero blocks]
\lean{FABL.tribes_zero}
\label{FABL.tribes_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.orFunction, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative integer $w$, the tribes function with zero blocks is the constant
function with value $+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-block negative probability]
\lean{FABL.tribes_neg_one_probability_zero}
\label{FABL.tribes_neg_one_probability_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribes, FABL.tribes_zero, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $w$, the uniform probability that the tribes function with
zero blocks takes the value $-1$ on the zero-dimensional Boolean cube is
$1-(1-2^{-w})^0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical size condition]
\lean{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate}
\label{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate}
\leanok
For natural numbers $w$ and $s$, the pair $(w,s)$ satisfies the tribes critical size
condition exactly when $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le \tfrac12$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical size]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b007}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate}
For each natural number $w$, the tribes critical size is the greatest natural number at
most $2^{w+2}$ that satisfies the tribes critical-size candidate predicate for $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical dimension]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b007}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
For each natural number $w$, the tribes critical dimension is the product of $w$ and the
tribes critical size at $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Critical tribes function]
\lean{FABL.tribesCritical}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b007}
\label{FABL.tribesCritical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.tribes, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
For each natural number $w$, let $s$ be the greatest size up to $2^{w+2}$ for which
$1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le \tfrac12$. The critical tribes function is the tribes Boolean
function with block width $w$ and $s$ blocks, on $sw$ coordinates, taking values in
$\{−1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size is a candidate]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_spec}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b007}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_spec}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate, FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $w$, the critical size is a candidate size:
$1-(1-2^{-w})^{s}\le 1/2$, where $s$ is the critical size.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear bound for tribes influence]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_tribes_le_two_mul_dimension}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_tribes_le_two_mul_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_dimension, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_of_hasDNFWidthLE, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ and $s$ be nonnegative integers, and form the tribes function on $s$ blocks of
$w$ signs each, taking the disjunction of the conjunctions on those blocks. Its total
influence is at most twice the number of input coordinates, namely $2sw$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean function $f$ on the $m$-dimensional sign cube, its mean as a real-valued
function equals the uniform probability that $f$ takes the value $1$ minus the uniform
probability that it takes the value $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
For any natural number $s$ and any vector $v\in\{-1,1\}^s$, let the OR function take
value $1$ when every coordinate of $v$ is $1$, and value $-1$ otherwise. Identifying
each sign with its real value, its output is $2\prod_{i=1}^s\frac{1+v_i}{2}-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinates in a tribe block]
\lean{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart}
\label{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart}
\leanok
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $T$ be a subset of the $s w$ coordinates arranged as
$s$ blocks of width $w$, and let $i$ be a block index. The frequency part of $T$ in
block $i$ is the set of positions $o$ in that block for which the coordinate $(i,o)$
belongs to $T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in a tribe frequency part]
\lean{FABL.mem_tribeFrequencyPart}
\label{FABL.mem_tribeFrequencyPart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $T$ be a set of indices among the $sw$ positions, let
$i$ be a block index among $s$ blocks, and let $o$ be a position among $w$ positions.
Then $o$ belongs to the frequency part of $T$ for block $i$ if and only if the position
corresponding to the pair $(i,o)$ belongs to $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Number of supported tribe blocks]
\lean{FABL.tribeFrequencySupportSize}
\label{FABL.tribeFrequencySupportSize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers and let $T$ be a subset of the $s w$ coordinates arranged
as $s$ blocks of width $w$. The tribe frequency support size of $T$ is the number of
blocks whose frequency part is nonempty.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Real-valued tribes formula]
\lean{FABL.tribes_toReal_eq}
\label{FABL.tribes_toReal_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.andFunction, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_orFunction, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{3}
For all nonnegative integers $w,s$ and every input $x$ in the Boolean cube of dimension
$sw$, the real-valued version of the tribes function satisfies
\[
 f(x)=2\prod_{i=1}^{s}\frac{1+a_i(x)}{2}-1,
\]
where $a_i(x)$ is the real value of the conjunction of the $i$th block of $w$
coordinates of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty Fourier coefficient of the conjunction function]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_empty}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.andFunction, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.mean_booleanFunction_eq_prob_one_sub_prob_neg_one, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_andFunction_eq_neg_one, FABL.uniformProbability_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a nonnegative integer, and define $f:\{-1,1\}^w\to\{-1,1\}$ to equal $-1$ at
the all-$-1$ input and $1$ elsewhere. Its empty-set Fourier coefficient, computed with
uniform expectation on the cube, is $\widehat f(\varnothing)=1-2\cdot 2^{-w}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty Fourier coefficients of the conjunction function]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_of_ne_empty}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_of_ne_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.Sign, FABL.andFunction, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{6}
Let $w$ be a nonnegative integer, and define $f:\{-1,1\}^w\to\{-1,1\}$ to equal $-1$ at
the all-$-1$ input and $1$ elsewhere. For every nonempty subset
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$, its Fourier coefficient with respect to uniform
expectation on the cube is $\widehat f(S)=-2\cdot 2^{-w}(-1)^{|S|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of the conjunction function]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.andFunction, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_empty, FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction_of_ne_empty}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a nonnegative integer, and define $f:\{-1,1\}^w\to\{-1,1\}$ to equal $-1$
when every coordinate is $-1$ and $1$ otherwise. For $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$, let
$\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$, with uniform expectation on the
cube. Then $\widehat f(S)=1-2\cdot 2^{-w}$ if $S=\varnothing$, and $\widehat
f(S)=-2\cdot 2^{-w}(-1)^{|S|}$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[AND function monomial average]
\lean{FABL.expect_one_add_andFunction_mul_monomial}
\label{FABL.expect_one_add_andFunction_mul_monomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.andFunction, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_andFunction, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $w$ be a natural number and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,w\}$. On the uniform sign cube,
let $A_w(y)=-1$ when every coordinate of $y$ is $-1$, and let $A_w(y)=1$ otherwise;
write $\chi_S(y)=\prod_{i\in S}y_i$. Then
\[
\mathbb E_y[(1+A_w(y))\chi_S(y)]=
\begin{cases}
2\bigl(1-2^{-w}\bigr),&S=\varnothing,\\
2^{1-w}(-1)^{|S|+1},&S\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tribes coordinate indexing]
\lean{FABL.tribesCoord}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b005}
\label{FABL.tribesCoord}
\leanok
For natural numbers $w$ and $s$, identify the $sw$ coordinates with pairs $(b,j)$ where
$b\in\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$ and $j\in\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$ by the usual indexing of a product of
finite sets. The coordinate map sends each index to its corresponding pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes coordinate inverse identity]
\lean{FABL.finProdFinEquiv_tribesCoord}
\label{FABL.finProdFinEquiv_tribesCoord}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $w,s$ and any index $i$ among the $sw$ coordinates, applying the
canonical pairing map from a pair of indices in blocks of sizes $s$ and $w$ to the pair
of coordinates associated to $i$ returns $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recovering a coordinate from its block]
\lean{FABL.inputBlock_tribesCoord}
\label{FABL.inputBlock_tribesCoord}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.inputBlock, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s,w\in\mathbb N$, let $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(sw)$, and write
$(a,b)\in\mathrm{Fin}(s)\times\mathrm{Fin}(w)$ for the pair corresponding to coordinate
$i$. For every $x\in\{−1,1\}^{sw}$, the $b$th entry of block $a$ is $x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Remaining coordinates in a true tribe]
\lean{FABL.TribesRestTrue}
\label{FABL.TribesRestTrue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.tribesCoord}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $i$ be a coordinate among the $s w$ coordinates
arranged in $s$ blocks of width $w$, and let $x$ be a sign assignment to those
coordinates. The rest of the block containing $i$ is true at $x$ if every position in
that block other than the position of $i$ has sign $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Other tribes are false]
\lean{FABL.TribesOthersFalse}
\label{FABL.TribesOthersFalse}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.andFunction, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.tribesCoord}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $i$ be a coordinate among the $s w$ coordinates
arranged in $s$ blocks of width $w$, and let $x$ be a sign assignment to those
coordinates. The other tribes are false at $x$ if, for every block other than the block
containing $i$, the AND of its coordinate signs equals $+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance of an unaffected input block]
\lean{FABL.inputBlock_flipCoordinate_of_ne_tribe}
\label{FABL.inputBlock_flipCoordinate_of_ne_tribe}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $s,w\in\mathbb N$, let $x\in\{−1,1\}^{sw}$, and let $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(sw)$ specify a
coordinate, whose block index is the first component of its corresponding pair in
$\mathrm{Fin}(s)\times\mathrm{Fin}(w)$. For any block $t\in\mathrm{Fin}(s)$ different
from that block, flipping coordinate $i$ in $x$ leaves block $t$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipping a coordinate outside a block offset]
\lean{FABL.inputBlock_flipCoordinate_of_ne_offset}
\label{FABL.inputBlock_flipCoordinate_of_ne_offset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $i$ index one of the $sw$ coordinates, and let $x$ be
a sign vector of length $sw$. If an offset $o$ among the $w$ positions differs from the
within-block coordinate of $i$, then flipping coordinate $i$ leaves unchanged the value
of $x$ at offset $o$ in the block containing $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[AND value when the other coordinates are negative]
\lean{FABL.andFunction_eq_of_restTrue}
\label{FABL.andFunction_eq_of_restTrue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.TribesRestTrue, FABL.andFunction, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.inputBlock_tribesCoord, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $w,s$ be nonnegative integers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^{sw}$, and choose a coordinate $i$
of this vector, corresponding to block $j$ and within-block coordinate $o$. If every
other coordinate of block $j$ equals $-1$, then the AND of block $j$ equals $x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipped AND value when the other coordinates are negative]
\lean{FABL.andFunction_flip_eq_of_restTrue}
\label{FABL.andFunction_flip_eq_of_restTrue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.TribesRestTrue, FABL.andFunction, FABL.andFunction_eq_of_restTrue, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.inputBlock_flipCoordinate_of_ne_offset, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w,s$ be nonnegative integers, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^{sw}$, and choose a coordinate $i$
of this vector, corresponding to block $j$ and within-block coordinate $o$. If every
other coordinate of block $j$ equals $-1$, then after flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$,
the AND of block $j$ equals $-x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign indicator identity]
\lean{FABL.sign_ite_eq_self}
\label{FABL.sign_ite_eq_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{3}
For every sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$, the value that is $1$ when $b=1$ and $-1$ otherwise
equals $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes value under block conditions]
\lean{FABL.tribes_eq_and_of_restTrue_othersFalse}
\label{FABL.tribes_eq_and_of_restTrue_othersFalse}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.TribesOthersFalse, FABL.TribesRestTrue, FABL.andFunction, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.tribes, FABL.tribesCoord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $i$ be a coordinate in the sign cube of dimension
$sw$, and let $x$ be an element of that cube. If every coordinate in the block
containing $i$, other than $i$, has sign $-1$, and every other block has AND value $+1$,
then the tribes function on $x$ equals the AND value of the block containing $i$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $w,s\in\mathbb N$, let $i$ be a coordinate of the cube of dimension $sw$, and let
$x\in\{\pm1\}^{sw}$. The tribes function is pivotal at $x$ in coordinate $i$ if and only
if every other coordinate in the block containing $i$ equals $-1$, and every block other
than the block containing $i$ has at least one coordinate equal to $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Outputs of the AND Function]
\lean{FABL.card_andFunction_eq_one}
\label{FABL.card_andFunction_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.andFunction}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $w$, the number of sign assignments on $w$ coordinates at which
the AND function has value $1$ is $2^w-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence of tribes]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_tribes}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_tribes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.booleanInfluence_eq_influence_toReal, FABL.booleanInfluence_tribes, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.tribes}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ and $s$ be positive integers, and form the tribes function on $s$ blocks of $w$
signs each, taking the disjunction of the conjunctions on those blocks. Its total
influence is $sw\,2^{-(w-1)}(1-2^{-w})^{s-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Critical threshold for tribes]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\leanok
For a natural number $w$, define the critical threshold to be $\frac{\log
2}{-\log(1-2^{-w})}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A critical inverse lies in a half interval]
\lean{FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc}
\label{FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $w$, $2^{-w}\in(0,1/2]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A critical base lies between zero and one]
\lean{FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo}
\label{FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $w$, the real number $1-2^{-w}$ lies strictly between
$0$ and $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of a critical logarithm]
\lean{FABL.criticalLog_pos}
\label{FABL.criticalLog_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $w$, $0<-\log(1-2^{-w})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A critical inverse is bounded by its logarithm]
\lean{FABL.criticalInverse_le_criticalLog}
\label{FABL.criticalInverse_le_criticalLog}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $w$, $2^{-w}\le -\log(1-2^{-w})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the critical threshold]
\lean{FABL.criticalThreshold_nonneg}
\label{FABL.criticalThreshold_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalLog_pos, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\difficulty{1}
For every positive integer $w$, the tribes critical threshold $\frac{\log
2}{-\log(1-2^{-w})}$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical threshold upper bound]
\lean{FABL.criticalThreshold_le_two_pow}
\label{FABL.criticalThreshold_le_two_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalInverse_le_criticalLog, FABL.criticalLog_pos, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $w$, the tribes critical threshold $\frac{\log
2}{-\log(1-2^{-w})}$ is at most $2^w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Candidate size threshold equivalence]
\lean{FABL.candidate_iff_cast_le_threshold}
\label{FABL.candidate_iff_cast_le_threshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate, FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo, FABL.criticalLog_pos, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\difficulty{5}
Let $w$ be a positive natural number and let $k$ be a natural number. The inequality
$1-(1-2^{-w})^k\le 1/2$ holds if and only if $k\le \frac{\log 2}{-\log(1-2^{-w})}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size and logarithmic threshold]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_floor_threshold}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_floor_threshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate, FABL.candidate_iff_cast_le_threshold, FABL.criticalThreshold_le_two_pow, FABL.criticalThreshold_nonneg, FABL.tribesCriticalSize, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_spec, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $w$, the critical size of tribes of width $w$ equals the
greatest integer not exceeding the logarithmic threshold $\log
2/\bigl(-\log(1-2^{-w})\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for a critical logarithm]
\lean{FABL.criticalLog_lower}
\label{FABL.criticalLog_lower}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $w$, rac{1}{2^w}+rac{1}{2}\bigl(rac{1}{2^w}\bigr)^2 \le
-\log(1-2^{-w}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for a critical logarithm]
\lean{FABL.criticalLog_upper}
\label{FABL.criticalLog_upper}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $w$, $-\log(1-2^{-w})\le \frac{2^{-w}}{1-2^{-w}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Error in the critical size approximation]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
For a natural number $w$, define the critical size error to be $(\log 2)2^w$ minus the
critical size at width $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size error identity]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_main_sub_error}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_main_sub_error}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSize, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $w$, the critical size, viewed as a real number, equals $(\log
2)2^w$ minus the critical size error at $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size error bounds]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.candidate_iff_cast_le_threshold, FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc, FABL.criticalLog_lower, FABL.criticalLog_pos, FABL.criticalLog_upper, FABL.tribesCriticalSize, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_floor_threshold, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_spec, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}
\difficulty{6}
For every positive integer $w$, the critical size error lies in the interval $[\log
2/4,\,2]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size error order]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isTheta_one}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isTheta_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_mem_Icc}
\difficulty{4}
The critical size error is asymptotically of order $1$: its absolute value is bounded
above and below by positive constants for all sufficiently large $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Error in the critical dimension approximation]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
For a natural number $w$, define the critical dimension error to be $(\log 2)w2^w$ minus
the critical dimension at width $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical dimension as main term minus error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension_eq_main_sub_error}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension_eq_main_sub_error}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError}
\difficulty{1}
For each natural number $w$, let $s$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le 1/2$. Define the critical dimension as $ws$ and its error
as $(\log 2)w2^w-ws$. Then the critical dimension equals $(\log 2)w2^w$ minus its error.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical dimension and size errors]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError_eq}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError}
\difficulty{3}
For each natural number $w$, let $s$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le 1/2$, and define the critical dimension to be $ws$. Define
the size error to be $(\log 2)2^w-s$ and the dimension error to be $(\log 2)w2^w-ws$.
Then the dimension error equals $w$ times the size error.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic order of the dimension error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError_isTheta_natCast}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError_isTheta_natCast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError, FABL.tribesCriticalDimensionError_eq, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isTheta_one}
\difficulty{4}
For each natural number $w$, let $s$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le 1/2$, define the critical dimension as $ws$, and define
its error as $(\log 2)w2^w-ws$. As $w\to\infty$, this error is $\Theta(w)$; that is, it
is bounded above and below in magnitude by positive constant multiples of $w$ for all
sufficiently large $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical size error asymptotic]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isLittleO_two_pow}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isLittleO_two_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError, FABL.tribesCriticalSizeError_isTheta_one}
\difficulty{3}
The critical size error is little-o of $2^w$ as $w$ tends to infinity; equivalently, its
ratio to $2^w$ tends to $0$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
As the block width $w$ tends to infinity, the critical dimension is asymptotic to $(\log
2)w2^w$; equivalently, their ratio tends to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic ratio of critical dimensions]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_succ_div}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b002}
\label{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_succ_div}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension_isEquivalent_main}
\difficulty{5}
As the natural number $w$ tends to infinity, the ratio of the tribes critical dimension
at $w+1$ to the tribes critical dimension at $w$ tends to $2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical width error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalWidthError}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalWidthError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
For each natural number $w$, let $d_w$ denote the critical dimension used in the tribes
construction. Define the critical width error to be $w-\bigl(\log_2 d_w-\log_2(\log
d_w)\bigr)$, where the inner logarithm is the natural logarithm.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes critical width eq log sub loglog add error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalWidth_eq_log_sub_loglog_add_error}

\label{FABL.tribesCriticalWidth_eq_log_sub_loglog_add_error}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalWidthError}
\difficulty{1}
% dataset-pipeline: stub -- prose pending build_informal_statements.py
Statement pending regeneration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tribes critical logarithmic limits]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalLogLimits}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalLogLimits}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension_isEquivalent_main, FABL.tribesCriticalWidthError}
\difficulty{6}
For each natural number $w$, let $m_w$ be the greatest natural number $s\le 2^{w+2}$ for
which $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le \tfrac12$, taking $m_w=0$ if there is no such $s$. Set $D_w=m_w
w$ and $E_w=w-\bigl(\log_2 D_w-\log_2(\log D_w)\bigr)$. As $w\to\infty$, both
$\frac{\log D_w}{w\log 2}\to 1$ and $E_w\to 0$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
For each integer $w\geq0$, let $s_w$ be the greatest integer $s$ with $0\leq s\leq
2^{w+2}$ satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\leq 1/2$, taking $s_w=0$ if no such integer exists,
and set $D_w=s_w w$. As $w\to+\infty$ through integers, $\frac{\log D_w}{w\log 2}$ tends
to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical tribes dimension diverges]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_atTop}
\label{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_atTop}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension_isEquivalent_main}
\difficulty{3}
For each natural number $w$, let $s_w$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
such that $1-(1-2^{-w})^{s_w}\le 1/2$, and set $d_w=s_w w$. As $w$ tends to infinity,
$d_w$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical power relative error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
For each natural number $w$, let $d_w$ denote the critical dimension used in the tribes
construction. Define the critical power relative error to be $2^w\log(d_w)/d_w-1$, where
$\log$ is the natural logarithm.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical power relative error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError_isLittleO_one}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b002}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError_isLittleO_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tendsto_two_pow_mul_log_tribesCriticalDimension_div, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError}
\difficulty{3}
The critical power relative error is little-o of the constant function $1$ as $w$ tends
to infinity; equivalently, it tends to $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic dimension identity]
\lean{FABL.eventually_two_pow_eq_dimension_div_log_mul_one_add_error}
\label{FABL.eventually_two_pow_eq_dimension_div_log_mul_one_add_error}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_atTop, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalPowerRelativeError}
\difficulty{3}
For each natural number $w$, let $D(w)=w s(w)$, where $s(w)$ is the greatest natural
number at most $2^{w+2}$ satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^{s(w)}\le \tfrac12$, and let
$E(w)=2^w\log(D(w))/D(w)-1$. For all sufficiently large $w$,
$2^w=\frac{D(w)}{\log(D(w))}(1+E(w))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tribes critical probability deficit]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCritical, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.uniformProbability}
For each natural number $w$, define the critical probability deficit to be one half
minus the uniform probability that the critical tribes function on the sign cube of
dimension $d_w$ takes the value $-1$, where $d_w$ is the critical dimension used in the
tribes construction.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Critical tribes probability and deficit]
\lean{FABL.tribesCritical_neg_one_probability_eq_half_sub_deficit}
\label{FABL.tribesCritical_neg_one_probability_eq_half_sub_deficit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCritical, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $w$, the uniform probability that the critical tribes function
takes the value $-1$ equals $1/2$ minus its critical probability deficit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Critical probability deficit bounds]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate, FABL.candidate_iff_cast_le_threshold, FABL.criticalBase_mem_Ioo, FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc, FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit, FABL.tribesCriticalProbabilityDeficit_eq_pow, FABL.tribesCriticalSize, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_eq_floor_threshold, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_spec, FABL.tribesCriticalThreshold}

For every positive integer $w$, the critical probability deficit lies between $0$ and

\difficulty{5}
The critical probability deficit is big-O of the logarithm of the critical dimension
divided by the critical dimension as $w$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of critical size]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_pos}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalSize_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTribesCriticalSizeCandidate, FABL.criticalInverse_mem_Ioc, FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $w$, the critical size of tribes of width $w$ is
positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Critical tribes coordinate influence]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b003}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalSize}
For each natural number $w$, define the critical coordinate influence to be
$2^{-(w-1)}\bigl(1-2^{-w}\bigr)^{s-1}$, where $s$ is the critical tribes size for width
$w$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a positive integer. Let $s$ be the greatest integer at most $2^{w+2}$ for
which $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\leq 1/2$, and set $d=sw$. Form the tribes function on $d$ sign
coordinates by partitioning them into $s$ blocks of size $w$, taking the AND in each
block (equal to $-1$ exactly when every entry is $-1$), and then taking the OR of the
block outputs (equal to $1$ exactly when every block output is $1$). Every coordinate
has influence $2^{-(w-1)}(1-2^{-w})^{s-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence at critical tribes size]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_tribesCritical}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_tribesCritical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_tribes, FABL.tribesCritical, FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluence, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension, FABL.tribesCriticalSize, FABL.tribesCriticalSize_pos}
\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a positive integer. For the tribes function with block width $w$ and the
defined critical number of blocks, the total influence equals the critical dimension
times the critical-coordinate influence.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
For each natural number $w$, let $s_w$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
such that $1-(1-2^{-w})^{s_w}\le 1/2$. As $w$ tends to infinity,
$(1-2^{-w})^{\max(s_w-1,0)}$ tends to $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic critical dimension]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_dimension_div_two_pow_mul_log}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b002}
\label{FABL.tendsto_dimension_div_two_pow_mul_log}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tendsto_tribesCriticalDimension_atTop, FABL.tendsto_two_pow_mul_log_tribesCriticalDimension_div, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
\difficulty{3}
As the block width $w$ tends to infinity through the natural numbers, the ratio of the
tribes critical dimension at width $w$ to $2^w$ times the natural logarithm of that
dimension converges to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For each natural number $w$, let $s_w$ be the greatest natural number at most $2^{w+2}$
such that $1-(1-2^{-w})^{s_w}\le 1/2$, and set $d_w=s_w w$ and
$I_w=2^{-(w-1)}(1-2^{-w})^{\max(s_w-1,0)}$. As $w$ tends to infinity, $I_w
d_w/\log(d_w)$ tends to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate influence relative error]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluenceRelativeError}
\label{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluenceRelativeError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluence, FABL.tribesCriticalDimension}
For each natural number $w$, let $d_w$ be the critical dimension and let $I_w$ be the
coordinate influence used for the critical tribes function. Define the coordinate
influence relative error to be $I_w d_w/\log(d_w)-1$, where $\log$ is the natural
logarithm.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Relative error tends to zero]
\lean{FABL.tribesCriticalCoordinateInfluenceRelativeError_isLittleO_one}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p097-b003}

\difficulty{3}
For each natural number $w$, define the critical size as the greatest $s\le 2^{w+2}$
satisfying $1-(1-2^{-w})^s\le 1/2$, and define the critical dimension as $w$ times that
size. Let the coordinate influence be $2^{-(w-1)}(1-2^{-w})^{s-1}$, with $s$ the
critical size, and let the relative error be the coordinate influence times the critical
dimension, divided by the logarithm of the critical dimension, minus $1$. As
$w\to\infty$, this relative error is $o(1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Partition of a sign vector into blocks]
\lean{FABL.tribesBlockEquiv}
\label{FABL.tribesBlockEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.inputBlock}
For natural numbers $w$ and $s$, the coordinates of a sign vector of length $sw$ can be
identified bijectively with a family of $s$ sign vectors, each of length $w$, by
grouping the original coordinates into consecutive blocks of size $w$. The inverse
identification concatenates the blocks in their indexed order.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Block coordinates of the tribes equivalence]
\lean{FABL.tribesBlockEquiv_apply}
\label{FABL.tribesBlockEquiv_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.inputBlock, FABL.tribesBlockEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $w,s$, an input $x\in\{-1,1\}^{sw}$, and a block index
$i\in\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$, the $i$th block of the image of $x$ under the block equivalence
is the length-$w$ vector whose $j$th coordinate is the coordinate of $x$ indexed by the
pair $(i,j)$, for every $j\in\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Embedding coordinates into a product index]
\lean{FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\label{FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\leanok
For natural numbers $w$ and $s$ and an index $i \in \{0,\ldots,s-1\}$, the map sending
$o \in \{0,\ldots,w-1\}$ to the pair $(i,o)$, identified with its index in
$\{0,\ldots,sw-1\}$, is an injective map from $\{0,\ldots,w-1\}$ to $\{0,\ldots,sw-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Decomposition of a finite index set into blocks]
\lean{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart_biUnion}
\label{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart_biUnion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.mem_tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $w,s$ and a finite set $T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,sw-1\}$, partition the
indices into $s$ blocks of size $w$. In each block, take the offsets whose corresponding
indices belong to $T$, and map those offsets back to their indices in that block; the
union of these mapped subsets over all blocks is exactly $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Disjointness of tribe coordinate blocks]
\lean{FABL.disjoint_tribeOffsetEmbed}
\label{FABL.disjoint_tribeOffsetEmbed}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w,s$ be natural numbers, let $T$ be a finite subset of the pairs $(i,o)$ with
$i\text{ in }\text{Fin}(s)$ and $o\text{ in }\text{Fin}(w)$, and let $i,j\text{ in
}\text{Fin}(s)$ be distinct. For each coordinate $i$, take the offsets $o$ for which
$(i,o)$ belongs to $T$, and embed them into the $i$th coordinate block of $\text{Fin}(s
w)$. The resulting subsets for $i$ and $j$ are disjoint.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of block frequencies]
\lean{FABL.card_tribeFrequencyPart_sum}
\label{FABL.card_tribeFrequencyPart_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.disjoint_tribeOffsetEmbed, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart_biUnion, FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ and $s$ be natural numbers, and let $T$ be a subset of the $sw$ positions
arranged as $s$ blocks of $w$ positions each. For each block, count the positions of $T$
in that block. The sum of these counts over all $s$ blocks equals the cardinality of
$T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial factorization across blocks]
\lean{FABL.monomial_eq_prod_tribeFrequencyPart}
\label{FABL.monomial_eq_prod_tribeFrequencyPart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.disjoint_tribeOffsetEmbed, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart_biUnion, FABL.tribeOffsetEmbed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,w$ be natural numbers, let $T$ be a set of coordinates in an array of size $s w$,
and let $x$ be a sign assignment to that array. For each block $i$ among the $s$ blocks,
take the coordinates of $T$ lying in that block and view them as coordinates among the
$w$ positions. Then the monomial of $T$ at $x$ is the product, over all blocks, of the
monomial of that block's selected coordinates evaluated on the corresponding block of
$x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decomposing a finite-indexed function]
\lean{FABL.finArrowConsEquiv}
\label{FABL.finArrowConsEquiv}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$ and a type $\alpha$, a function from $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ to
$\alpha$ is equivalent to a pair consisting of its value at $0$ and its restriction to
the remaining $n$ indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of a product over a finite power]
\lean{FABL.expect_prod_finArrow}
\label{FABL.expect_prod_finArrow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.finArrowConsEquiv}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $s$ be a natural number, and for each $i<s$ let
$f_i:\alphato\bbr$ be a real-valued function. The uniform expectation over tuples
$(y_i)_{i<s}$ of the product $prod_{i<s} f_i(y_i)$ equals the product, over $i<s$, of
the uniform expectations of $f_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the tribes function]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_tribes_eq_prod}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_tribes_eq_prod}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.andFunction, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.expect_prod_finArrow, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.inputBlock, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_eq_prod_tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.signValue, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribes, FABL.tribesBlockEquiv, FABL.tribesBlockEquiv_apply, FABL.tribes_toReal_eq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $w,s$ be nonnegative integers, and let $T\subseteq[s]\times[w]$, viewed as a subset
of the $sw$ coordinates via the standard product indexing. For each block $i\in[s]$, let
$T_i\subseteq[w]$ consist of the coordinates of $T$ in that block. The Fourier
coefficient at $T$ of the real-valued tribes function is $-\mathbf
1_{T=\varnothing}+2\cdot 2^{-s}\prod_{i\in[s]}\mathbb
E_{y\in\{\pm1\}^w}\bigl[(1+\operatorname{AND}_w(y))\chi_{T_i}(y)\bigr]$, where
$\operatorname{AND}_w$ takes value $-1$ when all coordinates are $-1$ and $1$ otherwise,
and $\chi_{T_i}$ is the corresponding sign monomial.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product of tribe Fourier expectations]
\lean{FABL.prod_expect_one_add_and_tribeFrequencyPart}
\label{FABL.prod_expect_one_add_and_tribeFrequencyPart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.andFunction, FABL.card_tribeFrequencyPart_sum, FABL.expect_one_add_andFunction_mul_monomial, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue, FABL.tribeFrequencyPart, FABL.tribeFrequencySupportSize}
\difficulty{6}
For natural numbers $w,s$ and a set $T$ of coordinates in the product of an $s$-element
index set and a $w$-element index set, let $k$ be the number of indices whose
corresponding part of $T$ is nonempty. The product over all $s$ indices of the
uniform-cube expectation of $(1+\text{AND}(y))$ times the monomial indexed by that part
of $T$ equals $2^s(1-2^{-w})^{s-k}(2^{-w})^k(-1)^{|T|+k}$, where the AND function is
$-1$ exactly when every coordinate is $-1$.
\end{theorem}
